questions.prompt: A disease has prevalence \(0.01\). A test is positive with probability \(0.99\) for a diseased person and \(0.05\) for a non-diseased person. Find \(P(\text{disease}\mid\text{positive})\).
questions.answer: Let \(D\) be disease and \(+\) be a positive test. The evidence probability is \(P(+)=0.99(0.01)+0.05(0.99)=0.0594\). Thus \[P(D|+)=\frac{0.99(0.01)}{0.0594}=0.1667.\]

questions.prompt: A signal comes from source A with probability \(0.4\) and source B with probability \(0.6\). A click occurs with probabilities \(0.8\) and \(0.3\) respectively. Given a click, find the probability it came from source A.
questions.answer: The click probability is \(0.8(0.4)+0.3(0.6)=0.50\). Bayes' theorem gives \[P(A|\text{click})=\frac{0.8(0.4)}{0.50}=0.64.\]

questions.prompt: Machine 1 makes \(20\%\) of parts and has defect rate \(7\%\). Machine 2 makes the rest and has defect rate \(1\%\). Given a defective part, find the probability it came from machine 1.
questions.answer: Let \(M_1\) be machine 1 and \(D\) be defective. The defect probability is \(0.07(0.2)+0.01(0.8)=0.022\). Therefore \[P(M_1|D)=\frac{0.07(0.2)}{0.022}=0.6364.\]

questions.prompt: Rain has prior probability \(0.15\). Pavement is wet with probability \(0.9\) if it rained and \(0.2\) if it did not. Given wet pavement, find the probability that it rained.
A coin is chosen from a drawer. With probability \(0.6\) it is a biased coin with \(P(H)=0.4\); otherwise it is a coin with \(P(H)=0.8\). Given heads, find the probability the first coin was chosen.
questions.answer: Let \(B\) be the first coin and \(H\) be heads. The evidence probability is \(P(H)=0.4(0.6)+0.8(0.4)=0.56\). Bayes' theorem gives \[P(B|H)=\frac{0.4(0.6)}{0.56}=0.4286.\]

questions.prompt: A fault occurs with probability \(0.05\). An alarm sounds with probability \(0.95\) if there is a fault and \(0.02\) otherwise. Given an alarm, find the probability of a fault.

In an assessment, \(30\%\) of candidates are well prepared. A well-prepared candidate passes with probability \(0.6\), while another candidate passes with probability \(0.25\). Given a pass, find the probability the candidate was well prepared.
A batch is contaminated with probability \(0.12\). A quality test fails with probability \(0.85\) if contaminated and \(0.15\) otherwise. Given a failed test, find the probability of contamination.
questions.answer: The failed-test probability is \(0.85(0.12)+0.15(0.88)=0.234\). Bayes gives \[P(\text{contaminated}|\text{fail})=\frac{0.85(0.12)}{0.234}=0.4359.\]

questions.prompt: A component is old with probability \(0.7\). Failure probability is \(0.2\) if old and \(0.6\) if new. Given a failure, find the probability the component was old.

Team A has prior chance \(0.25\) of being the stronger team. If stronger, it wins with probability \(0.75\); otherwise it wins with probability \(0.35\). Given that Team A wins, find the probability it was stronger.
An email is spam with probability \(0.08\). A filter flags spam with probability \(0.9\) and flags non-spam with probability \(0.1\). Given that an email is flagged, find the probability it is spam.

An operator is trained with probability \(0.55\). A trained operator succeeds with probability \(0.65\), and an untrained operator succeeds with probability \(0.3\). Given success, find the probability the operator was trained.

A rare isotope is present with probability \(0.18\). A detector triggers with probability \(0.5\) when it is present and \(0.05\) otherwise. Given a trigger, find the posterior probability that the isotope is present.
questions.answer: The trigger probability is \(0.5(0.18)+0.05(0.82)=0.131\). Bayes' theorem gives \[P(\text{isotope}|\text{trigger})=\frac{0.5(0.18)}{0.131}=0.6870.\]

questions.prompt: A rejected item may be from batch X with prior probability \(0.33\). Rejection probability is \(0.4\) for batch X and \(0.7\) otherwise. Given rejection, find \(P(\text{batch X}|\text{rejected})\).
An infection has prevalence \(0.04\). A screen is positive with probability \(0.99\) if infected and \(0.01\) if not infected. Given a positive screen, find the probability of infection.
A device is in mode 1 with probability \(0.45\). A low reading occurs with probability \(0.3\) in mode 1 and \(0.8\) otherwise. Given a low reading, find the posterior probability of mode 1.

A signal is present with probability \(0.22\). A trigger occurs with probability \(0.88\) if the signal is present and \(0.18\) if absent. Given a trigger, find the posterior odds in favour of a signal.
questions.answer: First compute posterior probabilities up to a common denominator. Signal weight: \(0.88(0.22)=0.1936\). No-signal weight: \(0.18(0.78)=0.1404\). The posterior odds are \[0.1936:0.1404=1.38:1\] approximately in favour of a signal.

questions.prompt: An outage is reported. Sites are rural with probability \(0.65\). Outage probability is \(0.55\) for rural sites and \(0.25\) for non-rural sites. Given an outage, find the probability the site is rural.
A pressure drop is observed. A leak has prior probability \(0.1\). The pressure drop occurs with probability \(0.6\) if there is a leak and \(0.04\) otherwise. Find the probability of a leak.
questions.answer: The evidence probability is \(0.6(0.1)+0.04(0.9)=0.096\). Bayes' theorem gives \[P(\text{leak}|\text{drop})=\frac{0.6(0.1)}{0.096}=0.625.\]

questions.prompt: A mark can come from class I, II, or III with prior probabilities \(0.5,0.3,0.2\). A blue mark occurs with probabilities \(0.2,0.6,0.9\) in the three classes. Given a blue mark, find the probability it came from class III.
questions.answer: Use the multi-hypothesis denominator: \[P(B)=0.2(0.5)+0.6(0.3)+0.9(0.2)=0.46.\] The class III posterior is \[P(III|B)=\frac{0.9(0.2)}{0.46}=0.3913.\]
